scope: real test-time stereo experiment; In-The-Dark blocked by bandwidth, KITTI raw stereo fallback

rounds.hypothesis: run_000002.zip (837 MB) can be downloaded from the direct FTP link within the session budget, as the task brief assumed.
rounds.change: Measured the FTP link before committing: HEAD Content-Length; 30 s single-stream growth; 8-way parallel range requests; listed all official run sizes.
rounds.command: curl -I ftp://asrl3.utias.utoronto.ca/2020-vtr-dataset/UTIAS-In-The-Dark/run_000002.zip ; stat -c%s run_000002.zip (x2, 30 s apart) ; curl -r 8x2MB in parallel
rounds.metric_before_after: Before: assumed feasible. After: 874,634,312 B at 14 KB/s single-stream (434,176 B/30 s) and ~34 KB/s aggregate with 8 connections; smallest official run is 590 MB (run_000012). ETA 11.7-17.4 h single-stream. Only 1.6 MB landed, not a valid archive.
rounds.decision: pivot to fallback (KITTI raw stereo), document blocker

rounds.hypothesis: A hand-written SIFT stereo front-end on KITTI rectified images can produce enough real 3D-3D correspondences to feed the robust layer.
rounds.change: Added stereo_vo.py (detect, sub-pixel, ratio+mutual matching, analytic rectified triangulation) and a KITTI loader; first run returned ~0 correspondences, traced to an inverted mutual-NN index mapping in match().
rounds.metric_before_after: Before fix: 2 stereo matches from 3000/3000 keypoints, 0 3D-3D correspondences (while the ratio test alone had 1043 candidates). After fix: 229 correspondences per pair (median), 17.7% natural inlier rate.

rounds.hypothesis: Sparse left-right keypoint triangulation is too noisy at KITTI range (median inlier depth 28 m); dense StereoSGBM disparity should give more correspondences and lower depth bias.
rounds.change: Added frame_dense/correspondences_dense (SGBM numDisparities=128, block=5) and a sparse-vs-dense config in the runner; same 30 frame pairs, same robust layer.
rounds.metric_before_after: Correspondences median 229 -> 890 (3.9x), front-end time p50 0.49 s -> 0.35 s; inlier rate 17.7% -> 17.8%; GNC median rot 0.047 -> 0.052 deg, trans 0.694 -> 0.704 m; floor (GT-inlier Kabsch) 0.233 -> 0.239 m.
rounds.decision: keep dense (3.9x more data, same accuracy, faster); accuracy is front-end bound either way

rounds.hypothesis: SIFT should beat ORB for the temporal link on real rectified stereo, giving better robust-pose accuracy.
rounds.change: Switched the dense front-end detector to ORB (3000 features, nlevels=1) and reran the identical 30 pairs.
rounds.metric_before_after: SIFT -> ORB: correspondences median 890 -> 600, natural inlier rate 17.8% -> 20.7%, GNC median rot 0.052 -> 0.084 deg, GNC median trans 0.704 -> 0.739 m, floor trans 0.239 -> 0.202 m.
rounds.decision: keep SIFT (better rotation and translation; ORB's higher inlier rate does not translate into accuracy)

rounds.hypothesis: The 0.1 m translation criterion may simply be a threshold choice; sweeping the GT label / robust threshold c should reveal a c where success is attainable.
rounds.change: Swept c in {0.3, 0.5, 1.0} m for both GT labels and the robust layer, keeping correspondences fixed.
rounds.metric_before_after: c=0.3/0.5/1.0: natural inlier rate 5.9%/17.8%/69.7%; floor trans 0.129/0.239/0.473 m (success@0.25 m 100%/54%/0%); GNC trans 0.700/0.704/0.706 m and GNC rot 0.050/0.052/0.068 deg. Robust methods are c-insensitive while the GT floor is not.
rounds.decision: keep; reject the 'just relax c' hypothesis, report 0.1 m and 0.25 m success separately

rounds.hypothesis: On natural real correspondences the robust outer layer should match or beat fixed-budget RANSAC and reach the front-end noise floor at much lower runtime.
rounds.change: Ran Kabsch, RANSAC-1000, RANSAC-adaptive, IRLS-GM, GNC-GM on the same 30 real instances; added a GT-inlier-only Kabsch floor; validated stereo depth against LiDAR on frame 0 to attribute the residual bias.
rounds.command: /mnt/storage1/syk/venvs/opencv/bin/python run_kitti_stereo.py ; LiDAR-vs-SGBM depth check (inline script, results in README section 2)
rounds.metric_before_after: GNC 4.21 ms p50 / 6.46 ms p95 vs RANSAC-1000 81.3 / 118.0 ms (19.3x) and RANSAC-adaptive 2.66 / 14.12 ms; all methods 0% success at trans<0.1 m, median trans 0.70 m vs floor 0.24 m; median rot 0.052 deg (floor 0.071). Stereo/LiDAR depth ratio 1.000-1.061 over 3-60 m, so the 0.7 m forward-translation bias is not a disparity-scale bug.
rounds.decision: keep negative result: rotation solved, translation is front-end/consensus bound; the 0.1 m criterion is not reachable with this hand-written front-end
